headline: High: Roo Code’s default filesystem/network/MCP access can conflict with a local game-playing agent, while prompt-injection and leakage risks are limited by godot_rl_agents’ lack of I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no I/O surfaces or shared channel, so direct injection into it is unlikely. Roo Code can read/write workspace files and use MCP, so if the pair is bridged by manual copy-paste or a shared workspace, attacker-controlled content could be reinterpreted as instructions. The pathway is not default for the game-playing agent, so low fits.
conditions: IF the operator copies Roo Code output into a prompt consumed by godot_rl_agents
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace or MCP channel
mitigations: Disable copy-paste handoff between agents
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Strip instructions from any shared text artifacts
Require human review before forwarding outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: godot_rl_agents touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, while Roo Code reads workspace files and can egress broadly. Leakage is therefore mainly one-way from shared files or screenshots into Roo Code, not from the game-playing agent itself. The blast radius is small unless sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the VS Code workspace used by Roo Code
IF Roo Code is configured to send workspace contents or screenshots to a remote model API
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use a local-only model for Roo Code
Restrict workspace contents to non-sensitive files
Review browser/screenshot capture settings
requires-engineering: enforce workspace DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents is non-runnable and has no write or network permissions, but Roo Code can write files, modify git state, and share state via filesystem across instances. If the pair is co-located in one workspace, Roo Code can overwrite or race on files that the game-playing project uses. Uncertainty about the exact workspace layout pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem workspace
IF Roo Code edits files that godot_rl_agents also reads or generates
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Limit Roo Code to read-only mode for shared files
requires-engineering: add file locks or workspace isolation

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on outputs by editing files, running shell commands, and using browsers, so if it consumes artifacts from godot_rl_agents as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect code or actions. godot_rl_agents is a game-playing project with no documented verification or guardrails here, so its outputs should not be treated as trusted facts. The interaction exists in default workflows when outputs are manually forwarded.
conditions: IF outputs from godot_rl_agents are pasted into Roo Code tasks without verification
IF Roo Code is allowed to act on those outputs by editing files or running commands
mitigations: Require human verification before reuse
Ask Roo Code to cite source files before acting
Keep generated artifacts separate from executable code
Use a review step for any downstream action
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data classes are documented for godot_rl_agents, so compliance risk is limited. Roo Code does handle model provider API keys and can transmit workspace content to configured APIs, which creates policy exposure if regulated data is introduced. Because the other agent is not itself a regulated-data processor, this is a low-risk mismatch rather than a breach by default.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the Roo Code workspace
IF the configured model provider or MCP server is outside the required residency or retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use approved providers only
Disable unnecessary logging and retention
Review MCP server destinations
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
